title: client-habits-and-ask-sandpile-apr-2026
content:
Summary (topline)
- Small, recurrent asks from 12 enterprise accounts (Mar–Apr 2026) are aggregating into a fragility pattern: many low-cost requests that together create disproportionate operational load — a sandpile.
- Immediate suggestion: bundle 3 low-effort customer patches into a single 2-week spike owned by SE + SRE to reduce noisy tickets and collect telemetry; see quick plan below.

Observed client habits (evidence)
- Prefix-heavy workloads: 7 customers reuse long context prefixes repeatedly across requests (docs, templates). They often disable caching to avoid stale content.
- High retry rates (3–6 retries) around transient latency spikes — correlates with autoscaling thresholds.
- Embeddings usage spikes midday for two analytics customers; sudden burst patterns cause queueing and token throttles.
- Several customers ask for "deterministic short answers" and request lower temperature defaults via API — translates into many short, repeated generation calls.

Key asks surfaced (clustered)
- Request A: Stable prefix/KV cache that supports staleness TTL and manual invalidation (asked verbatim by multiple CS leads). Impact: reduces token counts and latency for prefix-heavy flows. Jira: CS-3421.
- Request B: Per-route cost breakdown and per-request estimate before charge (UX + API param). Customers want to surface cost to downstream billing — many take-home feature requests.
- Request C: Graceful fallback policy for model variants when dedicated pool is saturated (automated routing + notification).
- Request D: Short-session mode: fastest path for sub-128 token responses (quantization + lower batch windows).

Engineering notes / blockers (from ENG sync)
- KV cache design: current runtime supports prefix caching but lacks namespace isolation and TTL API. Implementation touchpoints: serving-runtime (cache layer), platform-engineering (routing), and console (invalidation button). ENG ticket: ENG-5897.
- Observability: need a per-token breakdown hook in tracing to attribute retries and autoscale events to customer traffic shapes.
- Autoscaler: current burst policy toggles are coarse-grained; adding a per-customer burst credit is non-trivial but could reduce retry storms.

Proposed near-term plan (2-week spike)
- Week 1: Instrument two customers (one prefix-heavy, one embeddings-bursty) to capture prefix frequency, average session length, and retry patterns. Owner: Ethan Caldwell.
- Week 1 deliverable: telemetry dashboard (console route) + synthetic replay harness for prefix caching.
- Week 2: Implement a lightweight TTL + manual invalidation API (backend flag + one-button in console prototype). Owner: Jordan Lin.
- Week 2 deliverable: rollout behind feature flag to 2 pilot customers, measure token reduction and latency delta.

Risk and mitigation
- Risk: Cache invalidation could cause customers to see stale content (legal contracts, pricing). Mitigation: default TTL conservative (1h) + manual invalidate in console + webhook on invalidation.
- Risk: Introducing per-route estimates impacts request latency (extra compute). Mitigation: provide async estimate endpoint and a conservative upfront heuristic in SDKs.

Customer-facing messaging (for CS)
- Short note: "Pilot: prefix-caching -> reduces repeated context tokens; will be available as opt-in feature with manual invalidation and audit logs. Expect 20–60% token reduction for common templates."
- Include brief FAQ on staleness and invalidation flows.

Open questions / decisions needed
- Product: do we expose per-customer burst credits or tune autoscaler heuristics globally? (Product + SRE)
- Security: require audit trail for invalidations? (Security team input)
- Pricing: discounted token accounting for cached-prefix hits? (Finance + Product)

Next steps & owners
- Marisol: coordinate pilot sign-ups and prepare CS messaging (due 2026-04-20).
- Jordan: prototype TTL + invalidate API (spike by 2026-04-25).
- Ethan: deck + telemetry dashboard (draft by 2026-04-22).
- Follow-up review in CS sync (2026-04-23).

Appendix: raw customer notes (anonymized snippets)
- "Our agents produce the same template every time; we're paying for tokens that repeat — can you cache the template?" — Enterprise A
- "We see sudden queues at 11am; engineers tell us it's autoscale. We keep hitting retry loops and paying for extra tokens." — Analytics customer B
- "Need simple button to clear cache when we update legal copy." — Finance platform C

References / artifacts
- Pilot proposal doc: CONF:client-ask-sandpile-2026
- Related Jira: CS-3421 (cache TTL / invalidate), ENG-5897 (observability hooks)
- Small patch PR: github.com/redwood-inference/patches/pull/214

Notes to self: keep the sandpile metaphor when talking to PMs — it's useful to show how many small asks form systemic load. Keep wording low-friction for customers ("opt-in pilot", "manual invalidation").
